0.headline: Hy-Tech Engineers IPO GMP nears 80% ahead of listing tomorrow; should you buy, sell or hold?
0.heading: Hy-Tech Engineers IPO GMP nears 80% ahead of listing tomorrow; should you buy, sell or hold?
0.intro: Hy-Tech Engineers is set for its stock market debut on September 1, with the company's shares commanding a strong premium in the grey market after its initial public offering (IPO) was subscribed more than 244 times during the four-day bidding period.
0.body:
Hy-Tech Engineers is set for its stock market debut on September 1, with the company's shares commanding a strong premium in the grey market after its initial public offering (IPO) was subscribed more than 244 times during the four-day bidding period.

The Rs 135.73-crore IPO, which opened on August 24 and closed on August 27, was subscribed 244.41 times overall. Investors placed bids for more than 443.49 crore shares against 1.84 crore shares on offer, according to NSE data.

The non-institutional investor (NII) portion was subscribed 402.29 times, while the qualified institutional buyer (QIB) category was booked 255.77 times. The retail portion received bids equivalent to 170.58 times the shares reserved for the category.

In the grey market, Hy-Tech Engineers shares were commanding a GMP of Rs 42 on August 31, as per InvestorGain. On the upper end of the price band of Rs 53, the figure translates into a potential listing gain of nearly 80 percent.

Read Also: Priority Jewels IPO: Issue subscribed over 10x on Day 2 so far; GMP stands at 22%

Investors must note that the grey market premium (GMP) is an unofficial indicator and can change before listing. It does not guarantee the actual listing price or returns.

The IPO comprised a fresh issue of Rs 60 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 1,42,89,450 equity shares. The price band was fixed at Rs 50-53 per share. The shares are scheduled to list on both the BSE and NSE on September 1.

Before the public issue opened, Hy-Tech Engineers raised Rs 40.72 crore from anchor investors through the allotment of 76.83 lakh shares at Rs 53 apiece. The anchor book included funds managed by WhiteOak Capital, along with other investors.

Check IPO News Here

Hy-Tech Engineers reported consolidated revenue from operations of Rs 189.40 crore for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, while consolidated profit stood at Rs 22.59 crore. Profit increased from Rs 19.62 crore in the previous year.

The company operates in the hydraulics industry and manufactures hydraulic fittings used across sectors including construction machinery, automobiles, farming machinery, injection moulding machines and hydraulic systems. It has more than four decades of operating experience in the industry.

Of the proceeds from the fresh issue, Hy-Tech Engineers plans to deploy around Rs 29.97 crore towards capital expenditure for expansion at its Kavathe, Shirwal and Pithampur Unit-I facilities. Another Rs 16 crore is earmarked for repayment of certain borrowings, with the balance intended for general corporate purposes.

Should you buy, sell or hold?

With Hy-Tech Engineers set to list on September 1, brokerage views point to a favourable long-term outlook.

Kantilal Chhaganlal Securities said the company has reported a 17.28 percent revenue CAGR and maintained EBITDA margins of around 22 percent over the past two years. The brokerage also highlighted its significant domestic market share and ability to generate around three times business from its investment amount, compared with about two times for peers.

"The company is likely to perform well in the long term. Expect Good Listing Gain. Allotted investors can hold medium to long term," Kantilal Chhaganlal Securities said.

Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers, meanwhile, pointed to Hy-Tech Engineers' more than four decades of experience, 11,000-plus SKUs, 170 direct customers and presence across sectors including construction, automotive, agriculture, railways and defence. At the upper price band, the IPO was valued at 22.25 times FY26 P/E and 12.15 times EV/EBITDA.

"While the valuation appears reasonable given the company’s growth prospects and established market position, therefore, we recommended to ‘Subscribe – Long Term' rating for the IPO," read the IPO note from Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers.

1.headline: Purple Style Labs IPO subscribed 5% so far on opening day; retail investors lead demand
1.heading: Purple Style Labs IPO subscribed 5% so far on opening day; retail investors lead demand
1.intro: Purple Style Labs, the parent company of luxury fashion platform Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, saw subdued investor participation on the opening day of its initial public offering (IPO), with the issue subscribed 5 percent by 11:25 am on August 31, according to data from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
1.body:
Purple Style Labs, the parent company of luxury fashion platform Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, saw subdued investor participation on the opening day of its initial public offering (IPO), with the issue subscribed 5 percent by 11:25 am on August 31, according to data from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The Rs 680-crore IPO received bids for 3,11,844 equity shares against 68,49,816 shares on offer. Retail investors led the subscription with 22 percent, while the non-institutional investor (NII) portion was subscribed 2 percent.

The IPO has a price band of Rs 546 to Rs 575 per share and will remain open for subscription until September 2. The issue comprises entirely a fresh issue of equity shares.

In the grey market, Purple Style Labs shares were commanding a premium of Rs 28 per share, according to InvestorGain. At the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 575, this translates into an indicative listing price of Rs 603 and a potential gain of about 4.87 percent.

Read Also: Priority Jewels IPO: Issue subscribed over 10x on Day 2 so far; GMP stands at 22%

GMP figures are unofficial and are based on activity in the unregulated grey market. They can change before listing and should not be treated as a guarantee of the actual listing price or returns.

Ahead of the public issue, Purple Style Labs raised Rs 306 crore from anchor investors on August 28. The company allotted about 53.22 lakh equity shares at Rs 575 apiece to 10 anchor investors, according to exchange filings.

The anchor book included names such as Morgan Stanley Asia, BofA Securities Europe, Integrated Core Strategies, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Jupiter India Fund, Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance Company, ITI Mutual Fund and Singularity Equity Fund I.

Of the net proceeds from the fresh issue, Rs 371.1 crore is proposed to be invested in subsidiary PSL Retail for expenditure related to lease liabilities for Experience Centers and back-end offices in India. Another Rs 138.9 crore is earmarked for sales and marketing expenditure, with the balance intended for general corporate purposes.

Purple Style Labs reported revenue from operations of about Rs 557.8 crore in FY26, up from Rs 489.9 crore in FY25. However, its net loss widened to about Rs 285.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 188.3 crore in the previous fiscal.

Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers for the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar.

Check IPO News Here

The shares are scheduled to be listed on the BSE and NSE on September 7.

About Purple Style Labs

Purple Style Labs operates Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop, an omnichannel luxury fashion platform offering designer products across women’s wear, men’s wear and other categories, with a focus on wedding and occasion wear.

The company sources products from a large network of designer brands and operates 14 Experience Centers, including 12 in metropolitan cities in India, alongside its online channels, events and exhibitions.

2.headline: Priority Jewels IPO: Issue subscribed over 10x on Day 2 so far; GMP stands at 22%
2.heading: Priority Jewels IPO: Issue subscribed over 10x on Day 2 so far; GMP stands at 22%
2.intro: Priority Jewels' initial public offering (IPO) continued to draw strong investor interest on the second day of bidding, with the Rs 91.5-crore issue subscribed 10.9 times by 11:00 am on August 31, according to data from the NSE.
2.body:
Priority Jewels' initial public offering (IPO) continued to draw strong investor interest on the second day of bidding, with the Rs 91.5-crore issue subscribed 10.9 times by 11:00 am on August 31, according to data from the NSE.

The issue received bids for 3,49,20,075 shares against the 32,02,500 shares available for subscription. Non-Institutional Investors (NIIs) led the bidding activity, with their portion subscribed 16.75 times. The retail investor category followed with a subscription of 14.34 times.

In the grey market, Priority Jewels shares were commanding a premium of Rs 45, according to InvestorGain. Against the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 200 per share, the premium indicates a potential listing gain of 22.5 percent.

Grey market premiums (GMPs) are unofficial indicators and can change depending on market conditions. They are not regulated by stock exchanges and do not guarantee the actual listing price or returns.

Read Also: ESDS Software IPO booked over 6x on Day 2 so far; GMP at 78%

The Priority Jewels IPO opened for subscription on August 28 and will remain open until September 1. The company has set the price band at Rs 190-200 per share.

The public issue consists entirely of a fresh issue of approximately 45.75 lakh shares. At the upper price band, the issue size stands at around Rs 91.5 crore. The IPO has a lot size of 75 shares, requiring retail investors to make a minimum investment of Rs 15,000 at the upper price band.

Before the IPO, Priority Jewels raised Rs 27.45 crore from four anchor investors through the allotment of 13.72 lakh shares at Rs 200 apiece. The company had also mobilised Rs 15.6 crore through a pre-IPO placement involving 8.25 lakh shares.

WhiteOak Capital Equity Fund and Sanshi Funds were the biggest participants in the anchor book, investing approximately Rs 8.65 crore each. Plutus Investment Trust and Khandelwal Finance invested around Rs 5.07 crore each.

Priority Jewels intends to deploy Rs 75 crore of the net IPO proceeds towards repayment of certain working-capital borrowings. The balance is earmarked for general corporate purposes.

The company reported total income of Rs 539.03 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 435.87 crore in FY25, representing a 24 percent increase.

Check IPO News Here

Profit after tax rose 68 percent to Rs 17.65 crore in FY26 from Rs 10.51 crore in the previous financial year.

The allotment of Priority Jewels IPO shares is expected to be finalised on September 2. The shares are tentatively scheduled to make their debut on the NSE and BSE on September 4

About Priority Jewels

Based in Mumbai, Priority Jewels manufactures lightweight diamond-studded gold and platinum jewellery. Its customers include independent jewellers as well as organised jewellery chains. As of June 2026, the company had more than 200 customers, including CaratLane Trading, Kalyan Jewellers India, Malabar Gold &amp; Diamonds FZCO, Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri and Senco Gold.
